source: Albrechtsberger, in Mann, The Study of Fugue (1958), p. 237, Ex. 219: 'Canon for five voices', the same tune with a fifth section, 'ad inferos, ad infe-ros'
transcription: As Ex. 218 (degree 0 = C4, quarter = 1, bar = 4), with five one-bar sections: bar 4 becomes E4 C4 G4 G3 (quarters) and bar 5 is C4 and a half rest. Read from the 600 dpi scan with the staff lines measured, and settled by the harmony where a half note's head was ambiguous: every section sounds at once, so beats 1-2 must be consonant (C5 E5 C5 over E4 or C4: C major) and beats 3-4 are G major (D5 B4 G4). The other reading of bars 1-3 (D5 F5 D5) makes sevenths and ninths against Ex. 219's added section.
